Class SimpleBoard

java.lang.Object
com.tetris.board.SimpleBoard
All Implemented Interfaces:
Board
public class SimpleBoard extends Object implements Board
Represents the core game logic board for Tetris.

This class manages the 2D grid of the game (the matrix), the active falling piece, collision detection, movement validation, scoring, and the "ghost" piece calculations. It serves as the bridge between the raw data and the GameController.

  • Method Details

    • isMoveValid

      private boolean isMoveValid(int[][] shape, int targetX, int targetY)
      Helper: Checks if placing the given shape at the target coordinates is valid.

      It checks for boundary violations (walls, floor) and collisions with existing locked blocks in the matrix.

      Parameters:
      shape - The 2D array representation of the brick shape.
      targetX - The target X coordinate (column).
      targetY - The target Y coordinate (row).
      Returns:
      true if the move is valid (no conflict); false otherwise.

    • attemptMove

      private boolean attemptMove(int dx, int dy)
      Helper: Attempts to move the current active shape by a given delta.

      If the move is valid, the currentOffset is updated.

      Parameters:
      dx - The change in X (horizontal).
      dy - The change in Y (vertical).
      Returns:
      true if the move was successful; false if blocked.

    • rotateLeftBrick

      public boolean rotateLeftBrick()
      Attempts to rotate the active brick to the left (counter-clockwise).

      This method implements a basic "Wall Kick" system. If the rotation is blocked by a wall or an adjacent piece, it attempts to shift the piece slightly (the "kick") to find a valid position for the rotation.

      Specified by:
      rotateLeftBrick in interface Board
      Returns:
      true if the rotation (with or without a kick) was successful; false if rotation is impossible.

    • createNewBrick

      public boolean createNewBrick()
      Spawns a new brick at the top of the board.

      Retrieves a new brick from the generator, sets it to the spawn coordinates, and checks for immediate collision (Game Over state).

      Specified by:
      createNewBrick in interface Board
      Returns:
      true if the new brick overlaps with existing blocks (Game Over); false if the spawn was clean.
